answers.answer: Shuffle the four Conflict III cards and place all four face down at the bottom; shuffle the nine II cards and deal five face down above them; shuffle the three I cards and deal one face down on top. Return unused cards to the box unseen; the shuffle-and-deal selects which I and II cards are used.
answers.evidence: Setup, lines 53, 60-68: face-down 10-card deck, I on top, five II, four III; return unused cards unseen.

answers.answer: In four-player play a human starts at 1 score; in three-player play at 0. Each starts with two Agents on the Leader and the third (Swordmaster) beside the board; three troops in their garrison and nine in supply; and 1 water.
answers.evidence: Setup, line 57: score 1 in a 4-player game, otherwise 0; two Agents, third beside board; three garrison troops, nine supply; take 1 water.

answers.answer: Yes, a player may Reveal while Agents remain. After Revealing, that player's turns are skipped for the rest of Player Turns, so they cannot later take an Agent turn that round. Reveal effects come only from cards revealed from the remaining hand, not Agent-turn cards. During Clean Up, all cards in front of the player from both Agent and Reveal turns go to the discard pile.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure, lines 91, 97-100: Reveal is allowed with Agents left; revealed cards only resolve Reveal boxes; all cards in front move to discard.

answers.answer: A resource granted by a Plot Intrigue played before Agent placement can pay the entry cost. A resource gained only after placement from the Agent card or destination cannot pay that same cost. One card sends one Agent using only one icon. A card with no Agent icons cannot be used on an Agent turn; it may only be revealed.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure, lines 91, 95: pre-placement Plot gains can pay; post-placement gains cannot; one Agent icon and no-icon restriction.

answers.answer: At a Combat space, you can deploy the three troops recruited that turn plus up to two more from your garrison: five total in this example. At a non-Combat space you cannot deploy units. Troops are recruited from your supply into your garrison; recruited troops eligible to deploy include those from the board space and played card this turn.
answers.evidence: Recruiting & Deploying, line 128: current-turn recruits plus up to two garrison units at Combat spaces; troop recruitment takes from supply to garrison.

answers.answer: A Spy Agent icon lets you send an Agent to a space connected to a post where you have a Spy, without recalling that Spy; a normal icon on the card can also authorize access where matching. Infiltrate recalls your Spy from a connected post to enter another player's occupied space, ignoring that occupancy; it cannot bypass your own Agent. Gather Intelligence recalls a connected Spy to draw a card, chosen immediately after Agent placement and before the space or card effects. The same Spy cannot pay both Infiltrate and Gather Intelligence.
answers.evidence: Special Rules, line 160: Spy Agent access does not recall; Infiltrate and Gather Intelligence descriptions and timing; cannot recall same Spy for both.

answers.answer: Strength is 2 troops × 2, plus one sandworm × 3, plus four swords × 1, totaling 11. If the final unit is removed, strength becomes 0. A player with no unit in the Conflict cannot participate in the Combat Intrigue window.
answers.evidence: Strength, lines 121-122: troops 2, sandworm 3, sword 1; no units means 0; Combat, line 103 requires at least one unit for Combat Intrigue.

answers.answer: Yes. Passing once does not prevent acting again if another player acts; the window closes after all players involved in Combat pass consecutively. After rewards, troops return to their supply (not garrison), and sandworms return to the bank.
answers.evidence: Combat, lines 103, 110: may act after earlier pass; consecutive passes close; troops to supply, sandworms to bank.

answers.answer: With two tied for first in a four-player game, each gets the second reward and the remaining players compete for the third reward; nobody wins or takes the Conflict card. With the same tie in a three-player game, each tied player gets second reward and there are no other rewards; nobody takes the card. A zero-strength player receives no reward.
answers.evidence: Combat, lines 105-110 and tie table lines 175-181; zero strength receives no reward.

answers.answer: One or more sandworms double the rewards you take; two worms do not quadruple them. Taking control of a location and battle icons on won Conflict cards cannot be doubled. For a reward allowing 3 spice for 1 VP, you may pay the cost a second time under doubling: pay 3 spice for the first VP, or 6 spice for 2 VP.
answers.evidence: Sandworm Reward Doubling, line 137: one or more double; control and battle icons excluded; optional reward cost may be paid twice.

answers.answer: When you win and take the Conflict card, first put it face up in your supply, then check for a match. Face-up Conflict or Objective cards with the same icon qualify. The matching pair must be flipped face down and scores 1 VP, so it is mandatory. During Endgame, a wild icon may match any one of the three icons in your supply; flip the pair for 1 VP.
answers.evidence: Combat, lines 107-108; Battle Icons, line 140: winner's check after card acquisition, matching face-up cards, must flip, wild at Endgame.

answers.answer: At 2 Influence, gain 1 VP; falling below 2 loses it, and reaching 2 again regains it. At 4, gain the printed track bonus, which is retained after falling below 4 and earned again on returning to 4; the first player to 4 also gains the Alliance and its 1 VP, which follows its holder. Tying the Alliance holder does not steal it: a challenger must rise above the holder. The separate FAQ trigger is a holder losing Influence after being tied; then the formerly tied opponent takes it, or if several were tied the former holder chooses the recipient.
answers.evidence: Scoring, line 153: 2 VP, 4 track bonus reversal, Alliance tied to holder, rise above to transfer; FAQ transfer trigger.

answers.answer: Persuasion is spent during the Reveal turn, before, between, or after Reveal effects. It may be pooled from multiple sources to buy one card and split from one source across cards. The Imperium Row is refilled to five, and you may buy a replacement immediately if able. An acquired card goes face up into your discard pile.
answers.evidence: Acquiring Cards, line 143: timing, pool/split, row refill/replacement purchase, discard destination.

answers.answer: At Makers, each empty Maker space gets one spice added to any accumulated bonus; visiting a Maker space collects all bonus spice there, including when choosing worms. Hagga Basin and Deep Desert offer base spice or, with Maker Hooks, one and two sandworms respectively. Hooks are required only when the summoning effect specifies them and are retained, not spent. A sandworm cannot go in a garrison; while Shield Wall remains it cannot be summoned to Arrakeen, Spice Refinery, or Imperial Basin. Once the Wall is removed, any Conflict is eligible.
answers.evidence: Makers line 113; Sandworms lines 131-134; Deep Desert/Hagga table lines 227,234.

answers.answer: At Recall at the end of a round, 10 or more VP for any player or an empty Conflict Deck triggers Endgame. Players first may play and resolve any Endgame Intrigue cards, then compare VP; the most VP wins. The rulebook resource tiebreakers in order are spice, Solari, water, then garrisoned troops.
answers.evidence: Scoring, line 150 and Recall line 116: Endgame trigger, Endgame Intrigue then most VP; listed tiebreakers.

answers.answer: Standard CHOAM starts with two contracts face up as offers and the remaining 18 face down in the bank. Add four CHOAM Imperium cards and four CHOAM Intrigue cards to their respective decks. Shaddam is optional. The ten contrasting-back contracts are for Rise of Ix compatibility and stay in the box; they are not part of this setup.
answers.evidence: CHOAM setup, lines 194, 206: two offers and 18 bank without Shaddam; four extra cards of each type; Shaddam optional; contrasting contracts excluded.

answers.answer: With CHOAM, the contract icon lets you take one of two face-up contracts and replace it with a face-up contract from the bank; if all contracts have been taken by players, it gives 2 Solari instead. A Harvest contract completes by visiting a Maker space and gaining the shown amount of spice during that turn in total, including other sources. Immediate completes upon taking it. Acquire The Spice Must Flow completes when you next acquire that card.
answers.evidence: Taking contracts line 196; Completing contracts lines 199-202.

answers.answer: No. If you take a contract for a space after already sending your Agent there this turn, you must wait until a future turn; you must hold the contract at the time you send the Agent. When completing it, announce it, gain its shown rewards, then flip it face down and leave it in your supply.
answers.evidence: Completing contracts, line 204: must have contract at placement; announce, gain rewards, flip down and retain in supply.

answers.answer: Standard two-player play uses one shared scoring Rival. The Rival gets the Ornithopter Objective; the other two eligible Objectives are dealt to the humans. First Player goes to the human whose card shows it, and alternates only between humans. Each round order is First Player → Rival → other human. The Rival never Reveals.
answers.evidence: Rival setup and Agent turns, lines 251-253: one shared Rival; objective/first player/turn order; never takes Reveal.

answers.answer: For an occupied destination, the Rival ignores it and reveals another Hagal card. A Place Spy card does not place an Agent: try an empty post of the specified type, ignore the placement if none exists, then reveal another Hagal card and continue the same Agent turn. Ignore ordinary board-space costs and effects; apply only revealed Hagal effects. If Hagal empties or Reshuffle appears, immediately reshuffle and continue.
answers.evidence: Rival rules, lines 253-257: occupied destination, Place Spy continuation, ignore normal space effects/costs, reshuffle behavior.

answers.answer: For three or four players, omit Objective cards whose printed player-count marking does not match, shuffle the eligible cards, and distribute one face up to each player; the card marked First Player determines who starts. Shaddam may be used only with the CHOAM Module, so he may not be chosen without CHOAM.
answers.evidence: Setup, lines 54, 56: choose Leader but Shaddam only with CHOAM; filter, shuffle and distribute eligible objectives face up, marked First Player.

answers.answer: The bank resources and sandworms are not limited; if the bank runs out, make a convenient substitution. By contrast, if your personal troop supply is empty, you cannot recruit more until some troops return to it. Resource payments for Solari, spice, and water go back to the bank; gains come from the bank, not another player's supply.
answers.evidence: Setup, lines 57-58: empty troop supply rule, bank not limited, take gains from bank and return payments.

answers.answer: The five phases are Round Start, Player Turns, Combat, Makers, Recall. At Round Start reveal a Conflict card, resolve the controlled-location defensive troop bonus if applicable, then each player draws five cards. If Endgame is not triggered at Recall, players return Agents to their Leaders, pass First Player clockwise, and begin the next round.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure, lines 85-88, 112-116: phase order, Conflict reveal then five-card draw, Recall procedure.

answers.answer: Yes. Board-space effects, Agent-box effects, and the Faction Influence advance may be carried out in any order. But entry requirements and costs must be met before placement and before any space or played-card effects resolve, so Influence from that visit cannot meet its entry requirement.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn, line 95: pay costs/meet requirements first, then effects and Influence in any order.

answers.answer: An optional arrow cost/effect may be paid and resolved only once per turn, not twice. Most card and space effects are mandatory; exceptions include effects stated as “may,” arrow costs that can be declined, and the optional black-X trash icon. Intrigue conditions and costs must be met to play the Intrigue.
answers.evidence: Arrows line 165; FAQ line 281: once-per-turn arrow exception; mandatory effects and optional exceptions; Intrigue conditions/costs.

answers.answer: Place a Spy from your supply on an unoccupied observation post connected to spaces, subject to any specified Agent-icon type. If you have no Spy in supply, you may first recall one of your Spies for no effect to free it. If the placement effect specifies an Agent icon that must be connected to the post, the post must meet that condition; otherwise you cannot place there.
answers.evidence: Special Rules, line 160: unoccupied post; recall Spy if supply empty; specific connected Agent icon requirement.

answers.answer: No, Infiltrate only bypasses another player's Agent, not your own. A Spy cannot be used without playing a card for an Agent turn to recall it. You cannot recall two connected Spies to Gather Intelligence twice on the same placement; you may use separate Spies for Infiltrate and Gather Intelligence.
answers.evidence: Special Rules line 160 and FAQ line 285: own occupancy exclusion; card still required; one Gather Intelligence, but distinct Spy for each different effect.

answers.answer: At controlled locations, the controller gains the separate visit bonus whenever any player visits, including if visitor and controller are the same person: 1 Solari at Arrakeen or Spice Refinery, 1 spice at Imperial Basin. Winning that location's Conflict transfers control by placing your marker and replacing an opponent's. When its Conflict is revealed, the controller may deploy one troop from supply directly to the Conflict, without visiting the space.
answers.evidence: Critical Locations line 161; board guide line 210 and table lines 225,237,244; defensive bonus is from supply.

answers.answer: In a three-player tie for second, each tied player gets the third reward; the first-place winner keeps the first reward and Conflict card, with no further rewards. In a four-player tie for third, those tied receive nothing. If three players tie for first, each gets the second reward; no one takes the Conflict card and no other rewards are given, even in a four-player game.
answers.evidence: Combat ties, lines 169-181: tie-for-second and tie-for-third outcomes; three tied first rule.

answers.answer: With three players at different positive strengths, first and second place receive their rewards; third receives nothing. A Rival counts as a player in the two-human-plus-Rival game, and ordinary third place receives nothing there as well, except that the third reward may be used for a tie for second.
answers.evidence: Combat, lines 105-106: ordinary reward ranks by player count; third reward in 2–3 players only for tie for second; Rival is third competitor, line 249.

answers.answer: Plot Intrigues may be played during your own Agent or Reveal turn; Combat Intrigues only during Combat and only if you have at least one unit in the Conflict; Endgame Intrigues at the end of the game. Keep unplayed Intrigues face down separate from your deck; after an Intrigue resolves, place it face up in a discard pile by the Intrigue Deck. If that deck runs out, shuffle its discard pile to make a new deck.
answers.evidence: Special Rules, lines 166, 286: timing, storage/discard, reshuffle exhausted deck.

answers.answer: An ordinary discard instruction discards a card of your choice from your hand and cannot discard an Intrigue unless specified. The separate trash-an-Intrigue icon lets you trash one Intrigue of your choice from your hand. Secrets takes one Intrigue selected at random from each opponent who has four or more Intrigues.
answers.evidence: Discarding line 168; Trashing line 146; Intrigue/Steal icon line 166.

answers.answer: A trash effect may remove a card from your hand, discard pile, or in play. Return ordinary trashed cards to the box; Reserve cards return to their Reserve stack. Trashing is optional unless it pays a cost or a card instructs you to trash itself. Trashing The Spice Must Flow does not remove the VP from its acquire effect; that VP is retained.
answers.evidence: Trashing line 146; Victory FAQ line 288: acquire VP retained after trashing.

answers.answer: An acquire-box effect resolves once at the moment the card is acquired. When you cannot draw because your deck is empty, shuffle the discard pile into a new deck and continue drawing. Unused Persuasion is lost at the end of your Reveal turn and cannot carry over.
answers.evidence: Acquire box line 183; Acquiring Cards line 143; reshuffle when deck empty.

answers.answer: Cards played on Agent turns and cards revealed during Reveal remain face up and in play until Clean Up, unless trashed earlier. Fremen Bond works if you have one or more other Fremen cards in play; two Bond cards can activate each other regardless of order played. They cease being in play at Clean Up.
answers.evidence: In play / Fremen Bond, line 184.

answers.answer: Recall Agent returns one of your other Agents on the board, not the one just sent this turn; the recalled Agent may be used on another Agent turn in the same round. A retreated troop goes from the Conflict to your garrison. “Retreat any number” includes retreating zero troops.
answers.evidence: Recall Agent line 185; Retreat line 186; FAQ line 287.

answers.answer: A freely chosen gain-two-Influence effect must put both Influence in one Faction; it cannot be split across two. An Alliance icon requires you to hold that Faction's Alliance token. A minimum-Influence effect requires the stated amount with its specified Faction.
answers.evidence: Influence rules line 163: free choice gain two cannot choose different Factions; Alliance and minimum Influence requirements.

answers.answer: If the holder loses Influence after being tied with two opponents, the former holder chooses which of those tied opponents receives the Alliance. If the holder falls to 3 or lower and nobody has 4 or more, return the Alliance token to the board and the old holder loses its VP.
answers.evidence: Scoring line 153 and FAQ line 282: former holder chooses among multiple tied opponents; return token if none has 4+.

answers.answer: A card drawn during Reveal is immediately revealed and used this turn. A card drawn after Reveal is kept for the next round, when the player draws five additional cards. A Plot Intrigue played earlier whose effect applies at Reveal stays face up until then, is used, and then discarded.
answers.evidence: FAQ Draw timing, line 286.

answers.answer: No. A “when you win a Conflict” Intrigue cannot be played after tying for first because no one wins. If you receive that Intrigue as a reward for an outright win, you may play it immediately.
answers.evidence: FAQ Combat and troops, line 287.

answers.answer: If final VP and all four listed resource tiebreakers are tied, the player who most recently took a Reveal turn wins. Scores may exceed 12 on the printed track.
answers.evidence: Victory FAQ, line 288.

answers.answer: No. You must fulfill all contracts you hold for the same space with that one Agent placement. The contract effects are another effect of that Agent turn and can be resolved in any order with the space and Agent-box effects; you must have held the contracts when you sent the Agent.
answers.evidence: FAQ Contract completion, line 283; completion rule line 204.

answers.answer: Shaddam does not begin with the set-aside Sardaukar contracts. Before the contract shuffle, set aside both; when acquiring a contract he may choose a set-aside Sardaukar contract instead of a generally available one. His Emperor of the Known Universe deployment restriction takes effect immediately when he plays Signet Ring to send an Agent, and lasts for that turn only, not the whole round.
answers.evidence: CHOAM setup line 194; Shaddam FAQ line 284 and Leader clarification line 188.

answers.answer: Feyd's token starts on the leftmost space of his Leader's Training track and stays on the rightmost space once it reaches it. Lady Jessica starts with her Lady Jessica side face up, not Reverend Mother Jessica. Reverend Mother Jessica may use her ability on the turn she flips.
answers.evidence: Leader clarifications, lines 188-189.

answers.answer: For Margot and Irulan, moving from 1 to 3 counts as reaching 2 even when passing it while gaining multiple Influence. They can reach 2 again later with the same Faction after losing Influence and regaining it, but moving down through 2 does not count. Clean Up moving Spacing Guild's Favor from in play to discard does not trigger its discard ability; only discarding it from hand does.
answers.evidence: Leader clarifications, line 188.

answers.answer: Accept Contract uses Spice Trade access, has no cost, always draws one card, and resolves the contract icon: without CHOAM or when all contracts are taken, gain 2 Solari; with available CHOAM contracts, take one. It is not a Faction space and grants no automatic Faction Influence. Dutiful Service uses Emperor access, has no cost, gains 1 Emperor Influence and resolves the same contract icon; it is an Emperor space, so that one automatic Emperor advance is counted once total.
answers.evidence: Board guide lines 212-230, especially shared contract rule and space table.

answers.answer: Arrakeen: City access, no cost, Combat space; visitor recruits one troop and draws a card, while controller receives 1 Solari. Fremkit: Fremen access, no cost, Combat space; gain 1 Fremen Influence and draw a card. Research Station: City access, costs 2 water, Combat space; recruit two troops and draw two cards.
answers.evidence: Board space table, lines 225, 232, 239.

answers.answer: Deep Desert uses Spice Trade access and costs 3 water; choose 4 base spice or, with Hooks, summon two sandworms. Hagga Basin also uses Spice Trade access and costs 1 water; choose 2 base spice or, with Hooks, summon one sandworm. At either space collect all accumulated bonus spice in addition to the choice. Hooks are retained and not spent.
answers.evidence: Board space table, lines 227, 234; Hooks not spent, line 133.

answers.answer: Both Sietch Tabr choices require City access, 2+ Fremen Influence, and no resource entry cost. Choice one: take Maker Hooks if you lack them, recruit one troop, and gain 1 water. Choice two: gain 1 water and optionally remove the Shield Wall. The second choice does not grant a troop.
answers.evidence: Board space table, line 243.

answers.answer: High Council uses Landsraad access, costs 5 Solari each visit, and is not a Combat space. On the first visit put your Councilor on an unoccupied seat and gain 2 Persuasion on each Reveal turn for the rest of the game. Subsequent visits give 2 spice, draw an Intrigue, and recruit three troops.
answers.evidence: Board space table, line 236.

answers.answer: Swordmaster uses Landsraad access and is not a Combat space. It costs 8 Solari before anyone gains Swordmaster and 6 after anyone does. Each player may take it only once per game. The third Agent becomes available this round and for the rest of the game. A Rival obtaining its Swordmaster also lowers the human cost to 6.
answers.evidence: Board space table, line 245.

answers.answer: Imperial Privilege uses Landsraad access; it requires 2+ Emperor Influence and costs 3 Solari. Its effects let you discard an Intrigue to draw an Intrigue, recall one of your other Agents, and draw a card. It does not automatically give Emperor Influence; it is a Landsraad space, not an Emperor Faction space.
answers.evidence: Board space table, line 238; Faction status distinctions, line 210.

answers.answer: Shipping uses Spice Trade access, requires 2+ Spacing Guild Influence, and costs 3 spice. It gains 5 Solari and 1 Influence with any one Faction; the Influence need not be Guild.
answers.evidence: Board space table, line 242.

answers.answer: Gather Support uses Landsraad access, is not Combat, and lets you choose to pay 0 or 2 Solari: recruit two troops either way, and paying 2 also gains 1 water. Spice Refinery uses City access, is Combat, and lets you pay 0 or 1 spice: gain 2 Solari free or 4 Solari if paying 1; its controller separately gains 1 Solari.
answers.evidence: Board space table, lines 233, 244.

answers.answer: Heighliner: Spacing Guild access, 5 spice, gain 1 Guild Influence and recruit five troops; Combat permitted. Desert Tactics: Fremen access, 1 water, gain 1 Fremen Influence, recruit one troop, optionally trash a card; Combat permitted. Sardaukar: Emperor access, 4 spice, gain 1 Emperor Influence, draw an Intrigue and recruit four troops; Combat not permitted.
answers.evidence: Board space table, lines 229, 235, 240.

answers.answer: Assembly Hall uses Landsraad access, costs nothing, is not Combat; draw an Intrigue, and if your Agent is there gain 1 Persuasion during your Reveal turn. Espionage uses Bene Gesserit access, costs 1 spice, is not Combat; gain 1 Bene Gesserit Influence, draw a card, place a Spy. Deliver Supplies uses Spacing Guild access, costs nothing, is not Combat; gain 1 Guild Influence and 1 water.
answers.evidence: Board space table, lines 226, 228, 231.

answers.answer: False Orders makes affected opponents move their Spy to an empty post not connected to your Agent's destination that turn. It may be played even if no enemy Spy is connected there. With Litany Against Fear, ignore its red box during Reveal, or when it gains an Agent icon and is played normally as an Agent card.
answers.evidence: FAQ, line 289.

answers.answer: Opponents cannot acquire the card removed by Manipulate. You may acquire it by other means, but without the 1-Persuasion discount. If not acquired by the end of your next Reveal, remove it from the game.
answers.evidence: FAQ Manipulate, line 289.

answers.answer: The Rival starts with a color, four Influence cubes at the bottom of tracks, three troops in its garrison and the rest in supply, two Agents in supply and Swordmaster beside the board, three Spies and 1 water in supply; its score and Combat marker start at 0. Shuffle House Hagal and retain the 2P Reshuffle card. The Rival can reach 10+ VP and trigger Endgame at Recall like a human; it can win by having the most VP.
answers.evidence: Rival setup and win condition, lines 249, 251.

answers.answer: When the Rival's combined Solari, spice, Intrigue cards, and water reach its printed Swordmaster value, each unit counts as one resource; it spends that many resources and takes its third Agent, available in the current round. It spends Solari first, then spice, then Intrigue cards, then water, keeping leftovers. The new Agent is immediately usable this round.
answers.evidence: Rival Resources and Swordmaster, line 261.

answers.answer: After obtaining Swordmaster, the Rival spends each set of 7 Solari, 7 spice, 3 Intrigue cards, or 3 water for 1 VP. It does not convert a mixed total of seven resources into a VP; the listed sets are exact individual resource thresholds.
answers.evidence: Rival Resources and Swordmaster, line 261.

answers.answer: When choosing Influence, the Rival chooses the Faction with least Influence, breaking ties by leftmost priority icon. It gains Influence VP at 2 and Alliance VP when holding an Alliance like a human; it does not get the resource/track bonus for reaching 4 Influence. A numbered Hagal Influence icon means that position in its Faction priority list.
answers.evidence: Rival rules, lines 257, 261, 275.

answers.answer: No. The Rival selects only the condition-matching destination; if it is occupied, it reveals a new Hagal card instead of using the other destination. The conditions are Guild Influence for Accept Contract/Shipping, and Conflict tier for Deliver Supplies/Heighliner.
answers.evidence: Rival Agent turns, line 253.

answers.answer: Yes, at every Combat space the Rival may deploy up to two available garrison troops even if the card recruited none. Troops recruited at a noncombat space go into garrison. A conditional 2+ Influence bonus not met does not prevent placing the Agent; it only means the bonus is not applied.
answers.evidence: Rival rules, lines 257-258: recruits deploy at Combat or enter garrison otherwise; always up to two garrison troops; conditional bonus does not block placement.

answers.answer: Unless a type is specified, the Rival places a Spy at the first available Faction observation post in its priority order; if all four are occupied, it ignores placement. Placing its third and final supply Spy immediately recalls its other two and triggers its Scheme. Rivals never recall Spies to Infiltrate or Gather Intelligence.
answers.evidence: Rival Spies and Schemes, line 259.

answers.answer: If the Scheme recruits troops before the Rival's Agent placement and it then visits a Combat space on the same turn, deploy those troops too. A Place Spy card does not send an Agent; if no legal post exists, ignore placement and immediately reveal another Hagal card to continue the Agent turn.
answers.evidence: Rival rules, lines 255, 259.

answers.answer: At Hagga Basin or Deep Desert with Hooks and a Conflict that permits worms, the Rival summons one or two worms respectively instead of base spice. Without Hooks, or if the Conflict is protected by Shield Wall, it summons none and takes base spice (Hagga 2, Deep Desert 4). It always collects all bonus spice there. Hooks are not spent.
answers.evidence: Rival Maker spaces line 263; Hooks retained line 133.

answers.answer: At Combat start, if the Rival has at least one unit deployed, reveal one Hagal card in turn order and add its bottom swords as strength; if Reshuffle appears, reshuffle and reveal again. Humans then have their normal Combat Intrigue window. A Rival with no unit deployed does not get this bonus.
answers.evidence: Rival Combat, line 275.

answers.answer: Yes: it gains control bonuses and the defensive troop when its controlled Conflict is revealed, wins Conflict cards and battle-icon VP normally, and doubles rewards with one or more worms. It always takes an optional Conflict VP if it can pay the resources or recall required Spies. It never takes contracts; even with CHOAM a contract reward gives it 2 Solari.
answers.evidence: Rival Combat, line 275.

answers.answer: During Reveal resolution, total and announce Combat strength and set the marker at any point; you may update it as needed while resolving. Strength over 20 is marked by flipping to the +20 side and starting again from the beginning of the track.
answers.evidence: Reveal Turn, line 99; Strength, line 123.

answers.answer: A Leader's Signet Ring ability activates when you play Signet Ring on one of your Agent turns, not merely when you reveal it. Card text can override the usual rules of the game.
answers.evidence: Setup, line 54; Overview, line 25.

answers.answer: A Recall Spy icon returns one of your Spies from an observation post to your supply, usually as a cost for an effect. The icon itself does not automatically Infiltrate or Gather Intelligence; those are separate effects available by recalling a Spy without a card for their stated purposes.
answers.evidence: Special Rules, line 160.

answers.answer: The trash-an-Intrigue icon trashes one Intrigue of your choice from your hand. An ordinary discard instruction instead discards a card of your choice from your hand and cannot be an Intrigue unless specified; discard does not mean trash.
answers.evidence: Trashing, line 146; Discarding, line 168.

answers.answer: Yes, a doubled reward that grants 1 Influence of your choice may be taken twice, with the same Faction or two different Factions. A single effect granting two Influence with free choice requires both gains with the same one Faction; it cannot split them.
answers.evidence: Sandworm Reward Doubling, line 137; Influence, line 163.

answers.answer: Resolve the Rival card's printed Signet Ring ability when Hagal shows a Signet Ring effect. It does not need a human Signet Ring card and never takes a Reveal turn; the Rival follows its printed Signet Ring and Scheme abilities as directed by its Rival card/Hagal effects.
answers.evidence: Rival overview/Agent turns, lines 249, 257; Rival never Reveals, line 253.

answers.answer: Maker Hooks icon: take a token from the bank if the Rival lacks one; if it already has Hooks, do not take another. Shield Wall removal: remove the Wall only if it has Hooks and the Wall remains; if it lacks Hooks, ignore it, and if the Wall is already gone it has no further effect.
answers.evidence: Rival Hooks and Wall icons, lines 265-273.

answers.answer: Secrets uses Bene Gesserit access, costs nothing, is not a Combat space, gains 1 Bene Gesserit Influence and draws one Intrigue from the Intrigue Deck. Each opponent with four or more Intrigues must give one selected at random; these come from opponents, not the deck.
answers.evidence: Board space table, line 241; Intrigue rules line 166.

answers.answer: Imperial Basin uses Spice Trade access, has no cost, and is a Combat space. The visitor receives 1 base spice plus all accumulated bonus spice; its controller receives 1 spice. If the visitor is also controller, that player receives both the visitor's spice and the separate 1-spice control bonus.
answers.evidence: Board guide lines 210, 237.

answers.answer: At Round Start, reveal a new Conflict from the top and place it face up next to the deck, on top of any Conflict cards left from earlier rounds. Resolve the controlled-location defensive troop bonus, then each player draws five cards; therefore the Conflict is revealed before the hand draw.
answers.evidence: Round Start, line 88.

answers.answer: Each human's four cubes start on the bottom spaces of the four Faction Influence tracks. The four Alliance tokens start on the marked areas of those tracks; no human starts holding an Alliance. The Shield Wall token is initially placed in the marked area below Spice Refinery.
answers.evidence: Setup, lines 52, 57.

answers.answer: The player with the First Player marker takes the first turn, then play continues clockwise, one turn at a time. A player who Reveals is skipped for the remainder of the phase; in three- or four-player play Player Turns end once all players have Revealed. Combat Intrigue priority begins with First Player and continues clockwise. An eligible player may play any number of Combat Intrigues before passing; the window ends after all involved players pass consecutively.
answers.evidence: Player Turns line 91; Combat line 103.

answers.answer: The steps are: Reveal Cards (reveal the remaining hand), Resolve Reveal Effects (resolve just those cards' Reveal boxes and acquire with Persuasion as desired), then Clean Up (move all cards in front to discard). Reveal effects may be resolved in any order, not necessarily card order.
answers.evidence: Reveal Turn, lines 97-100.

answers.answer: Shuffle each human's 10-card starting deck and put it face down in their supply; without CHOAM omit CHOAM-marked cards from Imperium and Intrigue decks, shuffle each separately face down, and deal five Imperium cards face up as the Row; put Prepare the Way and The Spice Must Flow in separate Reserve stacks. Each human Combat marker starts at 0; three Spies, Councilor, and Control markers remain in the player's supply; the four Influence cubes instead start at the bottom of the tracks.
answers.evidence: Setup lines 55-58; initial card states line 76; human components line 57.

answers.answer: During your Reveal turn, Persuasion can ordinarily buy any of the five Imperium Row cards or either Reserve card, Prepare the Way or The Spice Must Flow. Each card's cost is at its top right. Ordinary purchases happen during Reveal, not Agent turns.
answers.evidence: Acquiring Cards, line 143; Card anatomy line 93.

answers.answer: Ordinary Spy placement and Recall Spy icons are optional even when legal. A Shield Wall destruction icon may be declined. If destroyed, the Wall is removed for the rest of the game and cannot return in a later round.
answers.evidence: Special Rules, lines 160, 162: Spy actions optional; Shield Wall may be removed and cannot return.

answers.answer: Normally, an Agent destination must match one of the played card's Agent icons. A Spy connected to Shipping does not let a card with only City icon send an Agent to Shipping; it needs a matching ordinary icon or the card's Spy Agent icon with a Spy at a connected post. With the Spy Agent icon, it may send an Agent to any board space connected to a post where you have a Spy, without recalling that Spy.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn, line 95; Spy rules, line 160.

answers.answer: Yes. On an Agent turn you may first play a legal Plot Intrigue before placing the Agent; any resources it grants before placement become available and may pay the entry cost. Resources from the card used to send the Agent or from the destination occur only after placement and cannot pay that same entry cost.
answers.evidence: Player Turns cost timing, line 91; Agent Turn cost timing, line 95.

answers.answer: No. In two-player play, after both humans have Revealed, continue the Rival's Agent turns while it has Agents in supply. Combat begins only after both humans have Revealed and the Rival has used all Agents. The Rival never takes a Reveal turn.
answers.evidence: Player Turns, line 91.

answers.answer: When a Conflict card is revealed for a location the human already controls, the controller may deploy one troop from their supply directly to the Conflict; no Agent visit is required, and the bonus is optional. After rewards, all Combat markers reset to 0 before the next phase.
answers.evidence: Round Start line 88; Critical Locations line 161; Combat cleanup line 110.

answers.answer: Play one card from your hand face up in front of you and send one of your Agents from your Leader to an unoccupied matching space. Resolve that card's Agent box and ignore its Reveal box. You cannot reuse a card already in play or discard pile for this turn, and you cannot simply move an Agent already on the board; an Agent turn sends one from the Leader, except a recalled other Agent can later be used again as an Agent on another turn.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn, lines 95, 100; Recall Agent line 185.

answers.answer: No. Emperor of the Known Universe's deployment restriction applies immediately when Shaddam plays Signet Ring to send an Agent; resolving the board-space effects first cannot delay it.
answers.evidence: Leader clarifications line 188; FAQ Shaddam line 284.

answers.answer: With four players at distinct positive strengths and no worms, first place receives the printed first reward, second receives second, and third receives third; fourth place receives no reward. The first-place winner takes the Conflict card, then checks for a battle-icon match.
answers.evidence: Combat, lines 105-108: four-player ranks, zero strength no reward, winner takes card then checks match.

answers.answer: Players may choose a Leader or select one at random; random distribution is not required.
answers.evidence: Setup, line 54: each player takes a Leader (choose, or select at random).

answers.answer: An ordinary draw-a-card effect draws from your own deck. You may not choose a card directly from your discard pile; if your deck is empty, shuffle the discard pile into a new deck and continue drawing.
answers.evidence: Drawing cards, line 167.

answers.answer: Shuffle the House Hagal deck and place it near the shared Rival, retaining the 2P Reshuffle card in the deck. It is not removed.
answers.evidence: Rival setup, line 251: shuffle House Hagal and retain the 2P Reshuffle card.

answers.answer: All four Maker Hooks tokens begin in the common bank; normal setup gives none to a human. When acquired, a token moves from the bank onto that player's garrison.
answers.evidence: Setup, line 58.

answers.answer: The Combat marker must be adjusted when the Combat Intrigue resolves during the Combat Intrigue window if it changes deployed units or otherwise alters strength. The Reveal value is not fixed until cleanup; rewards use the adjusted strength shown on the track after all involved players pass consecutively.
answers.evidence: Combat, line 103.

answers.answer: Gained Solari, spice, and water come from the bank; the rules do not take them from another player's supply. Payments of those resources are returned to the bank.
answers.evidence: Setup, line 58.

answers.answer: Shuffle the standard contract tokens face down before exposing the two face-up offers; put the rest face down in the bank. Players do not choose the offers or preset the order of the bank; the shuffle randomizes them.
answers.evidence: CHOAM Setup changes, line 194: shuffle tokens face down, then flip two face up and put rest face down in bank.

answers.answer: If Shaddam is chosen, set aside both Sardaukar contracts before shuffling; only Shaddam can acquire these, and his Sardaukar Commander ability lets him choose one instead of a generally available contract. They do not start in his possession. Shuffle the remaining 18 standard contracts, expose two as public offers, and put 16 face down in the bank, with the two reserved contracts kept aside.
answers.evidence: CHOAM setup changes, lines 194 and 284.
